label: r3c1
name: r2c1 + 2 PPO epochs
hypothesis: Same network as r2c1, with ppo_epochs 2 instead of 4. Under the budget formula this gives about 1.86x more environment steps (about 190k), with a similar total number of gradient steps. r2c1's curve was still climbing steeply, so fresh designs should help more than reusing old samples. Refuted if the mean is below about 0.42, or if any seed collapses to DONE.
last_analysis: The observed target is shifted cyclically by X/2 along x, so it does not line up with the build. Adding a copy of the target rolled back by X/2 (r2c1, 0.48) was the breakthrough. Without it, runs collapse to DONE. The rest of the gain came from more samples per FLOP. With 2 PPO epochs, r3c1 reached 0.76 (0.82 and 0.69). With 1 epoch and 64-sample minibatches, r3c3 averaged 0.50, but its seeds diverged: 0.91 and 0.08. One epoch can reach a higher score but is unstable. Its seed-0 training success reached 0.89 and was still rising. Lower lr with more entropy (r2c2) slowed learning. Higher gamma (r3c2) hurt and made the agent stop early. In this last round I try to make the high-sample regime stable. Two levers: larger minibatches (less gradient noise) and a zero-initialised policy output (uniform start, less early drift toward DONE). One candidate isolates zero-init on the 2-epoch best.
